The data used in this study are based on the operating experience failure reports from calendar year 1998 through 2024 as reported in the Institute of Nuclear Power Operations (INPO) Industry Reporting and Information System (IRIS). The considered MOV failure modes are fail to open or close (FTOC), fail to operate or control (FTOP), and spurious operation (SO). The component reliability estimates and the reliability data are trended for the most recent 10-year period, while yearly estimates for reliability are provided for the entire study period. The following reliability trends in component failure probabilities and failure rates were identified for MOVs for the most recent 10-year period: • Low-demand MOV FTOC failure probability—decreasing • High-demand MOV SO failure rate—decreasing. The following engineering trends in component demands and failure events were identified for MOVs for the most recent 10-year period: • Low-demand MOV frequency of FTOC demands (demands per reactor year)—increasing • Low-demand MOV frequency of FTOC events (events per reactor year)—decreasing • High-demand MOV frequency of SO events (events per reactor year)—decreasing. v Page intentionally left blank vi CONTENTS ABSTRACT .................................................................................................................................................. v ACRONYMS ............................................................................................................................................... xi 1.
